title.rendered: Give Us This Day Our Daily Bread | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 4

excerpt.rendered: In first-century Judea, day labourers lived on one-day margins. The food on today’s table came from today’s work. That is the economic reality behind the fourth petition of the Lord’s Prayer.

content.rendered:
In first-century Judea, most of the common people were day labourers. They were hired in the morning, worked through the heat of the day, and were paid at sundown. If they were not hired, their family did not eat the next day. That is the economic reality behind the fourth petition of the Lord’s Prayer.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, October 6, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 4

Today’s Scripture

“Give us this day our daily bread.”
Matthew 6:11 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In first-century Judea, most of the common people lived as day labourers. They were hired at dawn in the village marketplace, worked through the heat of the day, and were paid at sundown. The Mosaic Law required employers to pay their workers before the sun went down, “for it is his wages, and his heart is set on it” (Deuteronomy 24:15). If a labourer was not hired on a given morning, his family did not eat the next day. The economy ran on one-day margins for most people. Flour was ground fresh. Bread was baked fresh. Nothing was stored. The food on today’s table came from today’s work and today’s provision. That is the economic reality Jesus was drawing on when He taught His disciples to pray, “Give us this day our daily bread.”

Notice what Jesus did not teach them to pray. He did not teach them to pray for next year’s security, next decade’s investments, or the retirement nest egg. He did not teach them to pray for abundance beyond today’s need. He taught them to pray for today’s bread. One day at a time. This is not a petition of poverty. It is a petition of dependence. Jesus is teaching the believer to walk in daily, moment-by-moment reliance on the Father’s provision, instead of trusting in stored resources, hoarded wealth, or future security as a substitute for present faith. The same lesson the Father taught Israel in the wilderness with the manna — gather what you need for today, trust Me for tomorrow — Jesus is teaching His disciples here. The Father is the Source. The Source is unchanging. Yesterday’s bread does not feed today’s body. Today’s bread comes from today’s Father.

The Passion Translation renders Matthew 6:11 with practical warmth: “We acknowledge you as our Provider of all we need each day” (Matthew 6:11 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Give us this day our daily bread” (Matthew 6:11 AMPC). Give us. Not sell us. Not reward us for our effort. Give us. The language is the language of a child receiving from a father who delights to give.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Short, specific, present-tense. Not “someday provide,” but “this day give.” Not generalised abundance, but today’s bread. The format trains the believer to pray with daily specificity rather than vague wishful thinking.

The Essence. This petition recognises the Father as the Source of everything the believer consumes. The farmer who grew the wheat was provided by the Father. The baker who milled the flour was enabled by the Father. The money in the believer’s pocket was supplied by the Father. All provision runs back to one Source. The petition acknowledges that reality.

The Authority. Jesus did not teach the believer to beg the Father for bread. He taught the believer to ask with the confidence of a child at a father’s table. The authority is in the covenant. Philippians 4:19 declares: “My God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.” The believer asks from a position of covenant provision, not from a position of desperate uncertainty.

The Assurance. Jesus told His disciples in the same Sermon on the Mount, “Do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink… for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things. But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you” (Matthew 6:25, 32-33). The assurance is total. The Father already knows. The Father will provide. The believer prays from assurance, not anxiety.

The Submission. This day. Not tomorrow. Not next year. The believer submits to the Father’s timing. The Father often gives what is needed exactly when it is needed, not before. Daily bread trains the believer in daily trust.

The Result. A believer who prays this way lives free from the slavery of financial anxiety. The provision is secured in heaven, released in time, and received by faith. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, pray for today’s bread with the confidence of a child whose Father has never missed a meal. Then go to work, do your part, and trust the One who feeds the sparrows and clothes the lilies to provide what you need, today, as He has promised.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done.

Specific Petition. Give us this day our daily bread. Supply all my needs today, Father, according to Your riches in glory by Christ Jesus. [Name the specific provision you need today.] I thank You for every provision You have already secured for me in Christ.

Submission. I trust Your timing. I trust Your amount. I trust Your way of providing. Today’s bread, from today’s Father, by today’s grace.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My Father is my Source. He supplies all my needs according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus. I live free from the slavery of financial anxiety. Today’s bread comes from today’s Father.

  • Philippians 4:19 (NKJV): My God shall supply all your need
